anchors.quote: Conditionally represent one activation of the pivot-selection expression as a one-hot QUBO over the eligible row indices col through n-1. The objective would have to select exactly the first index attaining the greatest Python abs(rows[i][col]) value. Any magnitude score, index tie-break term, and one-hot penalty must be proved to preserve that lexicographic result for every reachable state. Only line 13 is in scope; singularity checking, row swapping, elimination, back substitution, residual diagnostics, and report construction remain classical.

Encode n, col, and the current augmented-column values after all preceding swaps and elimination updates. One binary variable denotes each eligible row. A complete encoding must reproduce Python binary64 absolute-value and max behavior, including equal magnitudes, signed zero, and any nonfinite intermediate values reachable from finite inputs. Required coefficient precision, dynamic range, reversible or Hamiltonian-compatible data access, ancillary storage, and a sufficient one-hot penalty are unresolved.

Decode a one-hot row index and verify it against the original Python selection rule using the current row state. The quantum result may be used only if exact equivalence, including first-index tie behavior, is established. Invalid, infeasible, suboptimal, ambiguous, or uncertified samples cannot replace line 13. A semantics-preserving treatment of all unsupported states and failures remains an implementation obligation; merely declaring a classical fallback does not prove preservation.

The row-index domain is finite and a conceptual predicate could assert that an index is the first maximum, but evaluating that predicate requires exact comparison against all competing current pivots and faithful treatment of every reachable floating-point state. No reversible oracle, coherent data-access construction, resource bound, or deterministic error policy is supplied, so applicability is unresolved.
